title: FIR Filed Against Ex-TMC MLA Over Hurried Cremation of RG Kar Victim
excerpt: Former Panihati MLA Nirmal Ghosh and two associates face criminal charges for allegedly orchestrating the rushed cremation of the RG Kar rape-murder victim, as the Bengal government orders a fresh investigation into the case.
body:
• An FIR has been filed against former TMC MLA Nirmal Ghosh and two associates — Somnath Das and Sanjib Mukhopadhyay — for their alleged role in the hurried cremation of the RG Kar rape-murder victim
  • The victim's parents had moved a Kolkata court in May 2026, alleging the trio "hijacked" the body and rushed the cremation to prevent a second post-mortem examination
  • CBI investigators have confirmed the cremation was conducted with "unnecessary hurry" despite the family's request to preserve the body
  • On the second anniversary of the case, West Bengal Minister Dilip Ghosh confirmed a fresh inquiry is underway and promised punishment for the guilty

Criminal Charges Filed

In a significant development in the RG Kar Medical College rape-murder case, an FIR has been filed against former TMC MLA Nirmal Ghosh and two other individuals in connection with the alleged hurried cremation of the victim. The charges come nearly two years after the brutal crime that shocked India and triggered nationwide protests.

https://x.com/NewsArenaIndia/status/2087883916397154785

The victim's father alleged that the cremation was executed hastily to prevent a second autopsy and cover up crucial evidence. According to the complaint, the victim — a 31-year-old postgraduate trainee doctor — was found dead with severe injuries in the seminar hall of RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on August 9, 2024.

Court Plea Names Three Accused

The FIR follows a fresh application filed by the victim's parents before the Sealdah court in May 2026, naming Ghosh, Somnath Das, and local TMC functionary Sanjib Mukhopadhyay. The family alleged that the trio had "hijacked" the body from RG Kar Medical College and rushed the cremation process at the Panihati crematorium.

The plea stated there were attempts to prevent a second post-mortem examination, and the family was not provided all necessary documents before the cremation took place. During the May hearing, the CBI sought time until June to file a formal response.

"When we reached the crematorium, we found her body lying in front of the funeral pyre."

— Father of the RG Kar victim, describing the events at the Panihati crematorium

CBI Investigation and Earlier Questioning

The Central Bureau of Investigation had questioned Ghosh for seven hours in September 2024 after it emerged that he was present at both RG Kar hospital and the Panihati crematorium on the day of the crime. As the Panihati MLA, Ghosh claimed he accompanied the victim's family to the hospital as a "responsible elected representative."

However, CBI officials noted that Ghosh played "an important role in arranging the hasty final rites of the deceased doctor." The agency secured video footage from the Panihati crematorium showing the circumstances of the cremation.

Then-Leader of Opposition Suvendu Adhikari — now the state's Chief Minister — had publicly accused Ghosh and his associates of orchestrating the rushed cremation to prevent evidence from being uncovered. Adhikari pointed to the role of Sanjib Mukhopadhyay, a former CPM councillor who later joined the TMC, whose signature appeared on the victim's cremation certificate despite not being a family member.

Fresh Probe Under New Government

The case has gained renewed momentum under West Bengal's BJP government. On the second anniversary of the crime on August 10, 2026, West Bengal Minister Dilip Ghosh confirmed that a fresh inquiry is underway.

The RG Kar case had exposed deep institutional failures — from delayed FIR registration to questions about evidence preservation. The CBI's earlier investigation revealed that the police officer at the scene had deliberately registered the case as an unnatural death, failed to secure the crime scene, and allowed the rushed cremation despite the family requesting a second autopsy.

Civic volunteer Sanjoy Roy was arrested and later convicted in the rape-murder, but the victim's family has consistently maintained that the investigation failed to fully uncover the extent of institutional complicity in the aftermath of the crime.
